critique.good: Field names stay intact, and the example column begins within the initial viewport. The narrower table also requires the least horizontal scrolling of the three designs.
critique.problems: The email pattern becomes a tall, dense stack, making its syntax difficult to follow and creating a large first row. Several other patterns are fragmented, weakening the rhythm of the table.
critique.cause: The 135px Pattern column leaves only 114px for content. The 147px Field column preserves the row labels but leaves less of the viewport for the rule and example.

critique.good: The wider Pattern column makes several shorter expressions easier to read and reduces the height of the long email row. Field names and example values remain intact.
critique.problems: The email expression still forms a dense block, while the initial viewport shows only a sliver of the example column. Readers must scroll to compare rules with their outcomes.
critique.cause: The 180px Pattern column is a useful improvement over r0A, but Field and Pattern together occupy 327px. The remaining viewport width is too small to present an example.

critique.good: Patterns are much easier to scan, and the shorter, more even rows make the table feel calmer. The example and error columns have generous room for their content.
critique.problems: The initial viewport cuts through the Pattern column before reaching any examples, and the table requires substantial horizontal travel to reach error messages. The space gained for shorter patterns comes at a considerable scrolling cost.
critique.cause: The 300px Pattern column pushes the example column to 447px from the table's left edge. The 250px Error message column adds further width.

critique.good: Field names remain intact, and the pattern column gives most expressions a readable measure. All headers fit on one line, and no words split.
critique.problems: The email pattern is still fragmented, while several other rows contain large areas of empty space. The example and error columns require substantial horizontal scrolling.
critique.cause: The 220px pattern width wraps the longest expression across six lines; the 188px example and 190px error columns also contribute to row height and put the outcomes beyond the initial viewport.

critique.good: The narrower table reduces horizontal travel, and a glimpse of the example column appears in the initial viewport. Field names and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: The email pattern becomes a tall, difficult-to-follow block, and several shorter expressions also wrap more than they do in r1A. The taller rows weaken the table’s scanning rhythm.
critique.cause: Reducing Pattern to 180px leaves only 159px for text, producing a nine-line cell. The small reduction in scrolling comes at a substantial cost in height and pattern legibility.

critique.good: The wider pattern column makes the email expression easier to follow and keeps more of the shorter expressions together. It is the shortest of the three renders, with no mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The initial viewport cuts through the pattern column, and the example and error columns are even farther away. Some rows remain tall despite the extra pattern width, leaving visible empty space.
critique.cause: The 260px pattern width adds 40px of horizontal travel over r1A, while the 188px example and 190px error columns still determine the height of some rows.

critique.good: The field names stay intact, and the pattern column gives the long email expression a more manageable six-line shape. The table is the shortest of the three, with no reported mid-word splits.
critique.problems: The first viewport is dominated by Field and Pattern, so readers must scroll to compare the practical outcomes. The email pattern remains dense, and the 416px overflow makes cross-row comparison costly.
critique.cause: The 147px field column preserves row labels, while the 220px pattern column and the widths reserved for examples and messages push most outcome content beyond the viewport.

critique.good: The wider pattern column gives expressions more room and keeps the slug pattern on one line. Field names and headers remain intact.
critique.problems: The extra pattern width yields a taller table than r2A and increases horizontal scrolling. The taller slug row weakens the benefit of keeping its pattern on one line.
critique.cause: Increasing Pattern from 220px to 240px moves width away from Error message, which falls from 220px to 210px; the resulting wrapping increases the slug row height.

critique.good: The wider outcome columns give examples and messages more room, and some example content begins to enter the initial viewport.
critique.problems: The email pattern becomes an eight-line block, and other expressions fragment more. This makes the rule column harder to scan and produces a taller table despite the wider overall footprint.
critique.cause: Reducing Pattern to 190px reallocates space to Example valid and Error message. That helps the outcomes but leaves too little room for the long regex.

understanding.purpose: Document validation rules, valid examples, and error messages for customer onboarding fields.
understanding.reading: Readers locate a field, then read across its row to compare the rule with a valid example and the message shown when validation fails. Long pattern rows can absorb some natural wrapping in the example and message columns.
groups: Field and Pattern identify what is validated and define the rule.
Example valid and Error message show the rule's practical outcomes and should be easy to compare with it.
keep_intact: Field names, so rows remain easy to locate.
Regex tokens and expressions where possible, because inserted line breaks make syntax harder to follow.
Example values and identifiers, because their exact characters matter.
may_wrap: Long patterns across lines when necessary, with enough width to limit fragmentation.
Multiword examples at natural spaces where their meaning remains clear.

bad.why: The narrow pattern column forces the email expression into nine lines and makes that row disproportionately tall. The resulting height and fragmented expression are a poor exchange for the smaller horizontal scroll.

final.rationale: r2A gives the patterns and error messages enough space to keep the rows relatively compact while preserving complete identifiers and examples. Its first viewport shows the field names and nearly all of the pattern column, giving readers a useful starting point before they scroll to examples and messages. At 776px wide, it also asks for slightly less horizontal travel than several similarly compact alternatives.

general: Give columns width according to their content and role; equal widths are rarely the best starting point for mixed identifiers, code, examples and prose.
Judge horizontal scrolling against the readability and height gained by preserving meaningful text units.
Keep row identifiers readable and use row height to maintain clear associations across columns.
specific: The field column needs 147px to accommodate the longest identifier with the specified padding.
The long email pattern makes the pattern column particularly sensitive to narrowing, while the error messages also need room to avoid inflating row heights.

final.tradeoffs: r3B reduces horizontal travel by 20px at the cost of an extra 23px of table height. r3C shortens the tallest pattern and the table, but adds 40px of horizontal travel and leaves more of the pattern column beyond the initial viewport.
final.uncertain: The ranges are conservative design estimates, not browser-verified thresholds; small width changes can alter line breaks. Designers may reasonably prefer r3C if reading the longest expression matters more than minimizing sideways travel.

A.why: All four columns fit in the viewport, but field names, examples, patterns and error messages break into fragments. The resulting tall rows are difficult to scan.

B.why: Field names stay intact and most patterns are relatively compact, but the viewport cuts through the pattern column and the example and error columns require scrolling.

C.why: Field names remain intact and the example column begins in the viewport, but the narrow pattern column breaks expressions across many lines. The example is also cut off at the viewport edge.

D.why: Field names and most short patterns are readable within the initial viewport. Longer patterns wrap, while examples and error messages require horizontal scrolling.

E.why: Field names are intact, patterns have a useful amount of space, and the example column is signaled at the right edge. Longer patterns still wrap considerably, and examples require scrolling to read.

F.why: Field names are intact and the wider pattern column reduces wrapping, but the viewport cuts through several expressions and gives no view of the example column.

reviews.unsure: The supplied images do not show the complete off-screen portions of B–F, so I cannot fully assess the widths and wrapping of their example and error-message columns or the total scrolling distance.

A.why: Field names remain intact and most patterns are readable at first sight, though the slug pattern runs past the viewport. Examples and messages require horizontal scrolling.

B.why: All four columns fit, but the narrow widths split field names, examples, words, and regexes into fragments. The resulting tall rows are difficult to scan and compare.

C.why: Field names stay intact, but several patterns extend beyond the viewport, so reading even the first two columns requires scrolling. Examples and messages are farther away.

D.why: Field names are intact and a portion of the examples appears at first sight. The narrow pattern column breaks regexes into many lines, and the examples are cut by the viewport edge.

E.why: Field names and visible patterns fit within the viewport, with comparatively restrained wrapping. The examples and error messages still require horizontal scrolling.

F.why: Field names remain intact and patterns are mostly visible, but regexes wrap more than in E. Only a sliver of the examples appears at first sight.

reviews.unsure: The provided views show only the left portion of several layouts, so the widths and readability of their off-screen example and error-message columns are difficult to assess.
